verdicts.claim: The LAN build is a private preview, never the public pin, and its words say the game opens a network link (the kit stops if that line is gone).
verdicts.what_is_true: lan_kit.mjs:195 exits if lan_words.txt lacks 'opens a network link between the two PCs' (same check at a8bc66e2:182). The sentence is in the 'What this is' paragraph, not the first line, and the check runs after the export and shortcuts are written (lan_kit.mjs:106-117), so a failed run still leaves a playable folder with no READ ME. The pin 257a766c has no net/. desktop-package refuses net/ in the three desktop presets, but the Web preset at HEAD (export_presets.cfg:11) does not exclude net/*.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a real condition that works for a private build.
verdicts.fix: Move the words check before the export so a failed run leaves nothing playable. Correct 'the first line' in lan-v1.md:104. Add net/* to the Web preset, or say the guard covers desktop only.

verdicts.claim: No machine is a target during development, and minimum specs are measured and set before launch.
verdicts.what_is_true: ADR 0013 (Orb, 2026-11-01), lines 8-10, says exactly this. It is a performance planning decision with no player-safety or legal content. Setting minimum specs before launch would also fill any store field for them; I did not check Valve's rule on that.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It adds a store-gate row that no safety check can pass or fail. The cost is a little worry, nothing more.
verdicts.fix: Retire it from the safety records and keep it on Performance & Platform's pre-launch checklist.

verdicts.claim: Any text the public will see is written with care and seen by Orb before it is used.
verdicts.what_is_true: vision.md:951 records Orb's ruling: forward-facing writing seemed 'rushed and bizarre', so it is to be written with care and seen by Orb first. That is Orb's quality direction for copy, not a safety rule. Side finding: the public README.md:7 still says 'The hosted build is offline for now' while /play/ serves a playable build of 257a766c. The README last changed on 2026-10-12 (92c9c94f).
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Filed as a safety rule, it suggests public text is kept reviewed, which hides that the public README misstates the live build.
verdicts.fix: Move the rule to Orb's creative direction and Marketing's process. Separately, correct README.md:7 to describe /play/ as it is now.

verdicts.claim: Use the ™ mark only once the title is settled and in use, and never ® or 'registered' before a registration exists.
verdicts.what_is_true: The basis is real: the USPTO allows the registered symbol only with a federal registration. TM may be used without filing, so 'TM only once settled' is a stricter margin. git grep finds neither symbol anywhere in the committed tree outside docs/, and the store drafts carry the rule.
external: https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/basics/what-trademark (accessed 2026-11-07): 'You may only use the registration symbol with the trademark for the goods'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a sound pre-store rule with no current breach.
verdicts.fix: Keep it in Legal's store-copy screen. Optionally note that TM is lawful before the title is settled.

verdicts.claim: Testimonials must be real: friend connections stated, never passed off as independent reviews, no undisclosed solicited or keyed Steam reviews, no keys, gifts or favours traded for reviews, and quotes used only with permission.
verdicts.what_is_true: The FTC reviews rule has been in force since 2024-10-21, and the FTC's endorsement FAQ backs disclosing friendship connections, so Legal states the basis correctly. No testimonials exist: the table in store-copy-draft.md is empty. The '$51,744 per violation' figure is stale: the FTC raised it to $53,088 in 2025.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a correct marketing rule with nothing currently in breach.
verdicts.fix: Update or drop the penalty figure in go-to-market.md:171. Keep the rule in Legal's marketing screen.

verdicts.claim: Until Legal has read the Steam Distribution Agreement and Rules: the Steam description links to no other site, nothing Steam shows says 'free' or makes price claims about the browser build, nothing promises Remote Play or Steam-only features, and Remote Play is never called 'online multiplayer'.
verdicts.what_is_true: Valve's store page rules do bar links to other websites in the description. The 'free', price and Steam-only-feature limits are Legal's interim margin, honestly marked unconfirmed until the Distribution Agreement is read (B5). Valve's Remote Play page describes same-computer play and never calls it online multiplayer, so the wording rule is accurate. No Steam page exists.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page (accessed 2026-11-07): 'cannot use your store page to link to any other website'
https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/remoteplay (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Only the host needs to own and install the game'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): the core rule is Valve's own, and the rest is a labelled interim margin.
verdicts.fix: Legal reads the Steam Distribution Agreement and Rules before the fee (B5), then confirms or retires the interim limits.

verdicts.claim: Legal's four guides for Orb (licence, selling, company or individual in <state>, the stomp and ratings) are general information; the <state> fee and tax figures are unverified and must be checked on the state's site and by a lawyer and an accountant, and an LLC limits liability only if money and records are kept separate.
verdicts.what_is_true: review-log.md:174 and the guide (lines 3 and 7) say this. It is business-formation advice for Orb, not release safety. One figure checks out on the state's own site: an <state> LLC annual report costs $100. The $100 filing fee appeared only in search snippets and was not opened.
external: https://sos.<state>.gov/business/pages/dont-be-misled.aspx (accessed 2026-11-07): 'limited liability company (LLC) annual report is only $100'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An open 'risk' row on the store gate that is really Orb's business paperwork, which keeps it on safety lists until a lawyer and an accountant are paid.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Orb's business to-do list (homework) with Legal as adviser, and mark the annual-report fee as checked.

verdicts.claim: Keepsakes: rename Jar of Ash; Fused Sand Chip keeps 'blast' only; no paid hidden rewards (ln03).
verdicts.what_is_true: The rename is already done. rewards-words.md v2 (2c493910, 2026-10-18) and the parked keepsakes.json use 'Sky Jar' and 'Blast Sand Chip', so the row's 'Open until renamed' is stale. Keepsakes are a parked draft that is in no build, and the name is a tone call. ln03 guards a real loot-box concern, but the game sells nothing.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A stale open row keeps a finished tone fix on the store-gate list and suggests unfinished Legal work.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-158 in the review log. Keep ln03 as Legal's monetisation rule in case anything is ever sold. The tone of names belongs to Narrative and Orb.
verdicts.belongs_to: Narrative (Orb's creative direction); ln03 to Legal

verdicts.claim: The lost-graphics note stays below the gate's buttons and never above the warning or changes the gate; the boot bar moves forward only, shows real progress and makes no promise.
verdicts.what_is_true: The note slot comes after the gate's buttons, AI line and About link (tools/site-interim.mjs:103-107). It is built only when tools/site.json sets "crumbs": true, which neither HEAD nor 72a4d1e4 does, and the live /play/ carries none. The boot bar (boot.gd:141, 314) moves by shader jobs done, in whole percents, but exists only at HEAD, not in pin 257a766c. I did not check the small-phone layout.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a working placement rule, switched off on the live page.
verdicts.fix: None needed. Keep check-site-interim's crumbs check, and run the gate layout check when crumbs are switched on.
verdicts.belongs_to: Tools (site) and Rendering (boot line); Legal condition

verdicts.claim: Legal's cleared lines (flash notice, lock line, two buttons, AI line, privacy line) stay in English in every locale until Legal clears each translation, and the tools keep them byte-identical.
verdicts.what_is_true: pseudo.mjs --self-test passes when run today (output saved). The tool leaves Legal's lines unaltered in the pseudo-locale, but its byte-identity assertion covers only two terms.json lines, not all five. No real locale exists, so the rule binds nothing yet. An English-only flash warning in a translated build would also leave non-English players without a warning they can read.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a sound guard with a narrower test than claimed.
verdicts.fix: Extend the self-test to assert every line in page-fixed-lines.md. Before any locale ships, get Legal-cleared translations of the flash warning rather than relying on the English fallback.

verdicts.claim: At least 4 Steam screenshots must be marked suitable for all ages, which is Legal's call because the game shows violence.
verdicts.what_is_true: Valve's Graphical Assets page says you 'should' mark at least four screenshots, and only ones that really are suitable for all ages. Shots with violence should not be marked. If none are marked, the game may be left out of some placements, such as the front-page hover. It is a store-visibility recommendation, not a requirement and not a safety matter.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/assets/standard (accessed 2026-11-07): 'you should mark at least four screenshots'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It turns a visibility tip into a must, which could block store prep or push a violent game toward staging all-ages shots.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record to 'should, for visibility' and move it to Marketing's store-asset list. Legal still reviews which shots are marked.

verdicts.claim: No implied endorsement by Valve, itch.io, platform holders, Godot, Anthropic or Suno, and no platform or engine logo unless its brand rules allow it.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule guards a real false-endorsement risk and is in force in the drafts. The README and site code have no 'powered by', 'endorsed', 'in partnership' or 'approved by' wording, and the tree holds no logo files outside docs. Godot is named only in its MIT notice (site-interim-owner.json:50). I did not check whether the engine's default boot splash shows its logo or read any brand's rules.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed): a sound rule with no current breach.
verdicts.fix: None now. Legal reads the brand rules when a logo is first proposed.

verdicts.claim: PlayStation needs a legal entity (sole traders accepted in Europe only), so nobody is told a console version is coming.
verdicts.what_is_true: Platform's own doc marks the entity and sole-trader rule as [S] secondary (stores-and-consoles.md:5, 47). I could not check it: partners.playstation.net shows nothing without a login. Not promising a console version is marketing honesty and business planning, not release safety, and no console port exists.
external: https://partners.playstation.net/ (accessed 2026-11-07): only the page heading is shown without login; no primary rule found
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: an unverified platform fact sits on a safety list and in Orb's review list as if settled.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Performance & Platform and Marketing's stage-5 plan, and mark the entity rule unverified until it is read on Sony's partner site.

batch_notes: None of AC-213 to AC-225 is a release blocker. Seven are sound store, web or private-build rules with nothing in breach (CONFIRMED-MINOR, S4), five are business, taste or planning items filed as safety (MISFILED), and one overstates a Valve recommendation (AC-223).
Stale public text: README.md:7 says the hosted build is offline, but /play/ serves a playable build of 257a766c. README last changed 2026-10-12 (92c9c94f).
Stale record: RL-158 (review-log.md:180) is 'Open until renamed', but the keepsakes were renamed on 2026-10-18 (2c493910).
lan_kit.mjs checks the words after exporting the game, so a failed run leaves a playable folder with no READ ME. The Web preset at HEAD does not exclude net/* (the desktop presets do).

External figures: the FTC penalty in go-to-market.md:171 is the 2024 amount ($53,088 since 2025). Valve's four all-ages screenshots are a 'should'. The PlayStation entity rule is secondary-only and unverified.
Command output saved as evidence/AC-213.txt to AC-225.txt. Besides git, grep and one curl GET of /play/, the only script run was the read-only pseudo.mjs self-test. No Godot or browser was used.
